Emitted as ``client.<namespace>.<name>.read() / .write(v) / .subscribe()``.

operations.description: What callers can do with the value.

One named (write, notify) characteristic pair on a BLE transport.

Channels live on the *transport*; commands select one via ``ble.<transport_id>.channel``.

notify.title: Notify

Per-(command, ble-transport) channel routing and behavior block.

``channel`` must name a channel declared on the BLE transport's ``channels:`` map.

channel.description: Name of the transport channel this command uses (one of the transport's ``channels``).
channel.title: Channel

codec.description: Payload codec class (``module:Class``) for this one command, replacing the transport's codec.

expects_response.title: Expects Response

timeout.description: Seconds to wait on this transport. Overrides the command's ``timeout``.

The generated SDK emits a ``default_ble_matcher(candidate)`` that returns ``True`` only when every present criterion
matches the advertisement.

manufacturer_id.title: Manufacturer Id

name_prefix.description: Match devices whose advertised name starts with this.
name_prefix.title: Name Prefix

service_uuids.description: Match devices that advertise all of these service UUIDs.
service_uuids.title: Service Uuids

channel.description: Name of the transport channel whose notifications carry this event.

DiscoverySpec.description:
Optional top-level discovery configuration.

Lists at least one transport-family sub-block. Each present sub-block drives generation of a corresponding
``make_<family>_scanner()`` and ``default_<family>_matcher()`` in the SDK's ``scanners.py`` module.

http.description: Where ``scan_http()`` looks for the device and how it confirms it.

DiscoverySpec.title: DiscoverySpec

Event.description:
Stateless device emission primitive: a subscribe-only stream.

Distinct from an attribute subscribe (which streams changes of a named, read/writable *value*): an event has no
stored state — it is a fire-and-forget emission (e.g. "button pressed", "recording started"). The handler declares a
single ``payload`` type; the generated facade exposes ``client.<namespace>.<event>.subscribe()`` (async-only).

audience.description: Audiences whose SDK includes this event. Each must be listed in ``device.audience``.
audience.title: Audience

ble.description: Channel wiring for each BLE transport, keyed by transport id.
ble.title: Ble

capabilities.description: Capability tags the device must report; the client refuses the event on devices without them.
capabilities.title: Capabilities

handler.description: Your handler class (``module:Class``) that declares the payload type.
handler.title: Handler

http.description: Stream or polling wiring for each HTTP transport, keyed by transport id.
http.title: Http

transports.description: Ids of the transports this event can use. Each ``http`` or ``ble`` one needs a wiring block below.
transports.title: Transports

HttpAttributeOp.description:
One HTTP read/write operation for an attribute — a command-shaped block.

Verbs are explicit, never assumed: a non-REST device that *writes* via ``GET`` (e.g. ``GET /setting?option=9``) sets
``method: GET`` with ``query_from_request: true``, exactly like a command.

query_from_request.description: Send the value's fields as URL query parameters instead of a JSON body.
query_from_request.title: Query From Request

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for a reply.
timeout.title: Timeout

HttpAttributeOp.title: HttpAttributeOp

HttpAttributeSpec.description: Per-(attribute, http-transport) wiring: the ops this attribute supports here.

read.description: How to read the value. Required when ``operations`` includes ``read``.

subscribe.description: How to get updates. Required when ``operations`` includes ``subscribe``.

write.description: How to write the value. Required when ``operations`` includes ``write``.

HttpAttributeSpec.title: HttpAttributeSpec

HttpAttributeSubscribe.description:
HTTP subscribe wiring for an attribute: native SSE, or explicit opt-in polling.

Polling is never a surprise default — ``mode: poll`` must supply an ``interval``. ``mode: sse`` opens one long-lived
event stream instead.

interval.description: Seconds between polls. Required for ``poll``; not allowed for ``sse``.
interval.title: Interval

mode.description: ``sse`` keeps one stream open for updates; ``poll`` repeats a request every ``interval`` seconds.
mode.title: Mode

path.description: URL path of the stream (``sse``) or of the request to repeat (``poll``).
path.title: Path

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for each request.
timeout.title: Timeout

HttpAttributeSubscribe.title: HttpAttributeSubscribe

HttpCommandSpec.description: Per-(command, http-transport) wire-format and behavior block.

codec.description:
Codec class (``module:Class``) for this one command, replacing the transport's codec. Use it when one command's
format differs from the rest, such as a binary download; the easy start is a subclass of ``HttpJsonCodec``.
codec.title: Codec

expects_response.description: Set ``false`` for fire-and-forget commands: a missing reply counts as success and the call returns ``None``.
expects_response.title: Expects Response

query_from_request.description: Send the request's fields as URL query parameters instead of a JSON body.
query_from_request.title: Query From Request

timeout.description: Seconds to wait on this transport. Overrides the command's ``timeout``.
timeout.title: Timeout

HttpCommandSpec.title: HttpCommandSpec

HttpDiscoverySpec.description:
Probe-list configuration for HTTP discovery.

Unlike BLE, HTTP discovery has nothing to listen for — the scanner must be told which URLs to probe. ``base_urls``
is therefore required whenever this sub-block is present.

base_urls.description: Addresses to check, e.g. ``http://192.168.1.1:8080``. Each one that answers and matches is a found device.
base_urls.title: Base Urls

probe_path.description: Path requested at each address to confirm the device, e.g. ``/v1/status``. Must work without logging in.
probe_path.title: Probe Path

server_header_prefix.description: If set, the reply's ``Server`` header must start with this.
server_header_prefix.title: Server Header Prefix

HttpDiscoverySpec.title: HttpDiscoverySpec

HttpEventSpec.description:
Per-(event, http-transport) subscribe wiring: native SSE, or explicit opt-in polling.

Identical shape to an attribute's subscribe block — an event *is* a subscribe-only stream — but kept as its own
model so the two primitives stay self-documenting. Polling is never a surprise default: ``mode: poll`` must supply
an ``interval``; ``mode: sse`` opens one long-lived event stream.

interval.description: Seconds between polls. Required for ``poll``; not allowed for ``sse``.
interval.title: Interval

mode.description: ``sse`` keeps one stream open for events; ``poll`` repeats a request every ``interval`` seconds.
mode.title: Mode

path.description: URL path of the stream (``sse``) or of the request to repeat (``poll``).
path.title: Path

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for each request.
timeout.title: Timeout

HttpEventSpec.title: HttpEventSpec

Transport.description:
A wire transport (BLE / HTTP / serial / etc.) plus its codec.

``codec`` is the default for every command on the transport (a per-command ``codec:`` overrides it). It is required
for every family except HTTP, which falls back to the runtime ``HttpJsonCodec`` when ``codec`` is omitted.

The optional ``family`` field tags the transport for cross-validation: when set, commands riding this transport must
supply the matching per-transport block (``http:`` for ``family=http``, ``ble:`` for ``family=ble``). Loopback /
unknown / null transports impose no such requirement (this preserves the lightweight test-fixture style used in unit
tests).

adapter.description: Your own transport class (``module:Class``). Omit to use the built-in ``HttpTransport`` or ``BleTransport``.
adapter.title: Adapter

auth.description: Handshake to run before ``session_required`` commands. Reserved; not used yet.

channels.description: BLE only: named pairs of characteristic UUIDs. Each BLE operation picks one by name.
channels.title: Channels

codec.description:
Class (``module:Class``) that converts requests and replies to and from the wire, used by every command on this
transport. Required unless ``family`` is ``http``, which defaults to JSON (``HttpJsonCodec``).
codec.title: Codec

enrollment.description: HTTP only: the device's login endpoint, built into the SDK's ``http_enrollment()``.

family.description:
Kind of connection. Decides which other fields the transport needs and which wiring block (``http:`` or
``ble:``) each operation on it needs.
family.title: Family

id.description: Name for this transport, e.g. ``wifi``. Commands, attributes, and events refer to it.
id.title: Id

interpreter.description:
Class (``module:Class``) that decides whether each reply means success. Omit for the default: HTTP status codes
for ``http``, every reply accepted otherwise.
interpreter.title: Interpreter

Transport.title: Transport

TransportAuth.description: Optional per-transport handshake recipe for session-required commands.

handler.description: Handshake class (``module:Class``) to run before ``session_required`` commands. Reserved; not used yet.
handler.title: Handler

TransportAuth.title: TransportAuth

TransportEnrollment.description:
Declarative first-run login the generated SDK bakes into its HTTP enrollment adapter.

Only the *static* wiring lives here (the login path plus which response field carries the token). Runtime secrets --
credentials, API keys -- never live in the manifest; callers inject them at runtime via the generated
``<family>_enrollment(login_payload=...)`` factory.

login_path.description: Path the SDK POSTs to in order to log in and get a token, e.g. ``/v1/auth/login``.
login_path.title: Login Path

token_field.description: Field in the login reply that holds the token. Omit to try ``token``, then ``access_token``.
token_field.title: Token Field

Vendoring.description:
Explicit overrides for the import-closure walker.

The walker auto-discovers most files; these knobs handle edge cases (dynamic imports, intentionally vendored extras,
exclusions).

exclude.description: Files, folders, or globs (relative to a source root) to leave out of the SDK.
exclude.title: Exclude

extra_include.description: Files, folders, or globs (relative to a source root) to bundle even though no code imports them.
extra_include.title: Extra Include
